# Valenzuela metal fabricator retires the clipboard count

Subtitle: A fixed-scope inventory build for an smb-mfg plant

## Executive summary

A family-run metal fabrication shop replaced stock cards with barcode intake
and guided cycle counts. The Saturday full count became a rolling per-line
shift, and purchasing now reorders from system stock.

## About the customer

A fabrication shop in Valenzuela serving construction-hardware distributors.
Manual stock cards, one purchasing officer, no MES.

## Challenges

- Counts drifted between the cards and the floor.
- Purchasing reordered from memory during peak months.
- Audit weekends burned overtime.

## Solution

An eight-week fixed-scope build: barcode intake at goods-in, guided cycle-count
routes, reorder alerts tied to on-hand stock, and a BIR-ready invoice export
built to the EOPT rule that every sale of ₱500 or more carries a registered
invoice [ev:C-1].

## Results

- The full-plant count moved from a weekend to a rolling per-line shift
  [vs: the pre-build clipboard count].
- Reorder decisions now start from system stock instead of memory.
- Delivery ran on the utilisation discipline the 2025 SPI benchmark reports
  for services firms [ev:C-2].

## Quotes

"The clipboard is retired. The counts match the system." — Operations head

## Future plans

Second-line onboarding and supplier barcode compliance next quarter.

## Call to action

Ask for the reference call and the scoping checklist. [CTA]
